heading: What `realtime` already enforces from `linear_scan: false`
text:
### What `realtime` already enforces from `linear_scan: false` [LNLS.2.3]

`realtime` does not imply `linear_scan: false` in full, but it **automatically
enforces a subset** of the `linear_scan: false` constraints — specifically the
ones where violation causes truly unbounded execution or allocation
(not merely a larger T_wcet).  The following `linear_scan: false` exclusions
are compile errors under `realtime` whether or not `linear_scan: false` is
declared:

| LNLS constraint | Why `realtime` also requires it |
|---|---|
| LNLS.3.2 — no novel strings | Intern table is locked after `go_live`; a novel string causes `DS_ERR_OOM` mid-firing. Must be a compile error, not a runtime error. |
| LNLS.3.5 — no sketch backends | O(n) compaction can trigger any time in the pump; cost is unbounded and cannot be included in T_wcet. |
| LNLS.3.7 — regex without `capacity` | O(L×P) where L is run-time length; unbounded without a declared `capacity`. |
| LNLS.3.8 — string ordering without `capacity` | O(len) strncmp; unbounded without a declared `capacity`. |
| LNLS.3.9 — JSON_PATH | Already blocked by the no-`json`-slots rule (LNLS.3.1); listed for completeness. |
| LNLS.3.11 — series scan without `capacity` | O(D) scan where D (series depth) grows with the event trace; unbounded without a sample cap ([LSER.13.14]) — already a compile error under `realtime` (`DS_VALIDATE_RT_SERIES_UNBOUNDED`). |
